nodes.summary: Substitute a context into the hole of another context.
nodes.title: Composition of process contexts

nodes.summary: One-hole lexical contexts, including guards, choice and replication.
nodes.title: One-hole lexical process contexts

nodes.summary: Structural congruence is sound under every observer context, with one-for-one reduction matching and immediate input/output barbs.
nodes.title: Structural congruence implies contextual barbed equivalence

nodes.summary: Strong barbed equivalence in every lexical process context. For capture-avoiding use, both hole processes must satisfy `Proc.ClosedAt 0`.
nodes.title: Contextual strong barbed equivalence

nodes.summary: Structural congruence survives every one-hole lexical context.
nodes.title: Structural congruence is closed under contexts

nodes.summary: Contextual barbed equivalence survives filling a context.
nodes.title: Contextual barbed equivalence is closed under contexts

nodes.summary: Every structural law is strongly barbed sound under capture-avoiding contexts, for locally closed hole processes.
nodes.title: Structural laws are barbed sound in capture-avoiding contexts

nodes.summary: Lexical and capture-avoiding filling agree for locally closed holes. This is the explicit admissibility condition for the contextual theorem.
nodes.title: Capture-avoiding and lexical filling agree on locally closed holes

nodes.summary: Capture-avoiding filling: each context binder shifts dangling names of the hole, while binders internal to the hole remain untouched.
nodes.title: Capture-avoiding filling of a process context

nodes.summary: Context composition agrees with iterated filling.
nodes.title: Filling a composed context is iterated filling

nodes.summary: Fill the lexical hole. Free constants are never captured; locally closed hole processes have no references into surrounding binders.
nodes.title: Lexical filling of a process context

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
